label: FY2026 Q4 (Jul–Sep 2026)
asOf: close of $338.32 on 2 Nov 2026, $328.85 after hours (Investing.com)
headline: Selling more than expected, earning less: memory prices start eating Apple's gross margin

points.t: December-quarter gross margin is guided to 45–46%, 2–3 points below this quarter; management blamed mainly memory prices and expects them to keep rising beyond December.
iPhone +17% and Mac +24%, yet iPhone, Mac and iPad were all supply-constrained; the new foldable iPhone Duo is sold out with no timeline.

points.b: AI money goes to R&D, not data centers
points.t: R&D rose 32% in a year; full-year capex was just $9.0B, 29% less than the year before.

reaction: Stock: closed at $338.32 (−1.8%) on report day and fell to $328.85 (−2.8%) after hours. Revenue and EPS beat, and the +7–10% December-quarter revenue guide would be the biggest quarter in company history; what the market focused on was gross margin guided down to 45–46% and management saying memory prices will keep rising after December. The stock is up about 24% this year and trades at about 38 times trailing earnings. Next-day close to be added. Consensus from Investing.com: EPS $1.99, revenue $113.38B.

segments.title: Revenue mix
segments.take: Growth came mainly from iPhone and Mac; iPad and wearables fell against strong launch comparisons and supply limits.

rows.why: A September-quarter record, with “strong double-digit” iPhone growth in Greater China. Still limited by advanced-node chip supply, which management says eases as more products move to 2nm.
An all-time high with a 76% gross margin. Guided to slow to +8–9% in December: third-party licensing and FX, plus the US court ruling on App Store link-out payments.
Management stressed that Macs can run AI models locally; the December quarter will be memory-constrained.
Tough comparison with last year's Watch SE3 and AirPods Pro 3 launches.
Supply limits plus last year's A16 iPad launch.

segments.note: Greater China revenue was $17.54B, +21%, a September-quarter record; +28% for the year. Over 2.5B active devices and over 1.5B paid subscriptions.

extras.title: Where it sits in the AI loop
extras.take: In this chain Apple is a buyer competing with AI data centers for the same parts: AI has taken a share of memory and advanced-node capacity. It doesn't build large AI data centers itself; its AI money goes mostly to R&D, and the payback has to come from paid services across 2.5 billion devices.

items.w: The CEO called memory costs “unprecedented”. To lock in supply, manufacturing purchase obligations rose $33B from June to September and inventory went from $5.7B a year ago to $14.5B. The same week Sandisk reported an 85% gross margin: what Apple pays extra, Sandisk earns.

items.b: Competing with AI chips for leading nodes
items.w: Management said September-quarter constraints came from advanced-node capacity and will ease with 2nm; December constraints on Mac and iPad come from memory. NVIDIA, Google's TPUs and Apple's chips all queue at TSMC.

Full-year capex was $9.0B, 29% less than the prior year, while Google, Amazon, Microsoft and Meta each spend over $100B a year. Apple keeps AI on device and in Private Cloud Compute, with server inference costs booked in services cost of sales. Asked what share runs on Google Cloud, management didn't answer.
R&D was $11.7B in the quarter, up 32% in a year; December-quarter opex is guided up 11–13% y/y, mostly for AI R&D according to management.

items.b: 2.5B devices as the AI front door
items.w: Siri AI launched in beta in September and expanded to five more languages in October. Server-side AI features will have usage limits, with extra access for purchase: the first time Apple prices AI features separately.

extras.title: Where growth comes from
extras.take: Apple grows through upgrade cycles and services: iPhone is accelerating, but memory prices mean each extra phone earns less. The variables are how much cost Apple can pass on, and whether AI becomes a new paid service.

items.w: 2.5B active devices and a record iPhone user base; Greater China +21%. Demand exceeds supply, and the December revenue guide already assumes “constrained supply”.
Management said June and September price increases, carry-in inventory and cheaper non-memory parts offset part of the memory increase. Asked about price elasticity, the CFO said it's “early”.
The foldable iPhone Duo is supply-constrained; the CEO acknowledged display issues, with a “very small percentage” returned. No date for supply to meet demand.
Apple guides only one quarter ahead: December-quarter revenue +7–10%, its biggest quarter ever, and Services +8–9%. No long-term services or margin targets.
Watch whether memory keeps rising and gross margin falls below 45%; whether iPhone volumes slow after price rises; the effect of App Store link-out rulings on services; FX.

valuation.take: Apple trades at about 38 times earnings, above 18 of its past 20 quarter ends. The price assumes profits keep growing steadily, but on December-quarter guidance EPS is only about 2% above a year ago: memory costs make it hard to turn revenue growth into profit growth.

scenarios.title: Three scenarios: FY2027 profits
head: Case
Revenue growth
Gross margin
EPS
P/E at price
scenarios.note: Bear: memory keeps rising and price increases hurt volume; base: revenue grows at the December-guide pace with gross margin near the December guide; bull: iPhone Duo and AI services drive upgrades and memory prices peak. Opex = FY26 + 12% (the December-guide growth rate), other income $1.2B, 17% tax, 14.4B shares (with buybacks). Base EPS is almost identical to FY26's $8.98. These assumptions are ours and are not forecasts.

pricezone.sub: FY27 EPS × our P/E; price at the 2 Nov close (before the report)
pricezone.why: The price is already above the bull case: buying now, all three scenarios lose money, the base case about 21% and the bear case about 43%. Near the $223 midpoint the base case gains about 20% and the bear case loses about 14%, a reward/risk of about 1.5; the $200 low end is close to the bear-case price. The base case uses 30x, close to its five-year median P/E of about 31x; no higher, because profit may not grow for two years.

history.title: Against its own past 5 years
history.note: About 38x now, above 18 of the past 20 quarter ends, against a median of about 31x; only in the second half of 2024 was it higher. We calculate it from SEC quarterly EPS and calendar quarter-end closes; fiscal and calendar quarters are a few days apart.

cash.title: Cash generation
cash.sub: R&D expense per quarter, $B (where the AI money goes)
cash.note: Operating cash flow was $28.1B this quarter, with $24B of buybacks and $3.9B of dividends. Full-year operating cash flow was $145.1B against just $9.0B of capex. Inventory rose from $5.7B to $14.5B in a year and manufacturing purchase obligations rose $33B from June to September: Apple is locking in memory early. Management dropped the net-cash-neutral goal; cash and debt are now managed separately.

Scenarios: opex $75.54B × 1.12 = $84.6B; EPS = (revenue × gross margin − opex + $1.2B) × 83% ÷ 14.4B; price = EPS × multiple, rounded
Historical P/E = quarter-end close ÷ TTM GAAP EPS (SEC XBRL); 2026Q3 uses $333.02 ÷ $8.97
valuation.next: Next report around late January 2027 (December quarter).

changes.now: John Ternus hosted his first call as CEO; Tim Cook is executive chairman.

changes.before: Gross margin was 50.1% last quarter, and memory wasn't named as the main pressure.
changes.now: Memory costs are “unprecedented”, the main reason December gross margin falls, and will persist beyond it.

changes.before: Apple Intelligence came free with devices.
changes.now: Server-side features such as Siri AI get usage limits, with extra access for purchase; server inference costs go into services cost of sales.

changes.before: Long-term goal of net cash neutral.
changes.now: Cash and debt managed separately; still “invest what we need, return the excess”.
